answer: Agents mapping falcon nests on the tundra and surveying a reef can share a voting quota per independently allocated IPv4 /24 block. Require signed authorization from the prefix holder and verify its allocation in the routing registry; subdividing or delegating that block must not mint extra quota. A thousand keys on one block still share one budget. Extra influence requires renting or buying more scarce address space, rather than inventing names. This raises clone costs but favors address-rich operators and does not prove unique people.
